item.title: OpenRouter Drops 3 Providers After Researchers Catch Months of Prompt Theft at AI Hosting Firms
item.description: Attackers stole data from inside three AI inference providers for months, and none of the three knew until researchers told them, the industrial cybersecurity company Dragos said this week. Some of the stolen requests were flagged as Zero Data Retention , the setting that is supposed to mean a prompt is never stored. OpenRouter , a gateway that routes customers' AI requests to a pool of third-party providers, said today that it has removed three providers from its platform, removed 125 endpoints from eligibility for Zero Data Retention, and notified all potentially affected customers. The findings showed no breach of OpenRouter itself, the company said. The earliest of the three breaches began in mid-July. The planted prompts were bait, but they were processed alongside real customer requests, and those were almost certainly copied too, the firm said. The finding comes from canary token research that seeded about two million prompts with unique web links and credentials ...

item.title: Researchers Demonstrate Ghostscript Sandbox-Escape RCE via Crafted File Uploads in Popular Apps
item.description: A now-patched flaw in Ghostscript allows a crafted file to escape the program's security sandbox and run commands on the server that processes it. Ghostscript is the interpreter that many Linux servers use to convert uploaded PDFs, PostScript files, and images into other formats, often without the application calling it directly. Security firm pwn.ai showed this week that ordinary upload, preview, and print features in about ten common applications could be tricked into feeding it such a file. The flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-125396 , was fixed on September 8, and there have been no reports of it being used in attacks. Getting a crafted file to Ghostscript is easy, because an application does not have to call it directly. A common image or document library such as ImageMagick, Pillow, libvips, or a Qt plugin will hand PostScript or EPS content to Ghostscript to render, even when the file is named .png, .jpg, or .pdf. A routine feature like making a thumbnail or cropping a pict...

item.title: A Single Malicious Webpage Let Researchers Hijack Meta Muse and Access Private Chats
item.description: A malicious webpage could extract a Meta Muse user's private conversations and stored memories from the assistant without triggering any approval prompt, researchers have shown. The same attack could be extended to reach the credentials Muse stores for the user's connected accounts. The work was a laboratory demonstration, not an attack on real users, and it stayed inside the individual user's cloud machine. NebuSec , the security firm that published it yesterday, says Muse's team has since fixed every weakness it describes. Muse is Meta's personal AI agent, launched on September 8, that works through the online accounts a user connects to it and can make purchases on their behalf. Each person's agent runs on its own cloud computer. There, a monitoring layer called Sentinel is meant to be the single gate for anything the agent sends out, and the passwords and tokens for connected accounts are supposed to stay beyond the agent's reach.

item.title: GnuPG Warns Critical GPGME Flaw Could Expose App Data via Malicious OpenPGP Keys
item.description: A malicious OpenPGP key with an unusually long user ID can trigger a critical memory bug in GPGME , the standard library that programs use to work with GnuPG. The GnuPG project warned yesterday that the flaw could be used to steal data from affected applications and has released fixed versions. The bug, tracked as CVE-2026-129975 , affects all software that uses GPGME before version 2.3.0, whether the library is loaded as a shared library, a Windows DLL, or statically linked into the program. Examples the project gives include most mail clients, many XMPP clients, Samba, and its own Gpg4win, GnuPG Desktop, and GnuPG VS-Desktop packages. The project has not reported any attacks exploiting the flaw, and it notes that remote code execution cannot be ruled out. Its example of a path to the bug is signed data sent to an application. item.title: Attackers' AI Agents Found a Zero-Day in Medical-Imaging Software and Gained Root Access
item.description: Suspected China-linked hackers used autonomous AI agents to find a previously unknown flaw in MONAI Label , an open-source medical imaging server, and gain root access to a university server, Amazon Threat Intelligence said this week. The flaw allows an attacker with no account to write files outside the server's storage folder, and it affects MONAI Label 0.8.5 and earlier in the default setup, which runs with no login enabled. The maintainers have merged a fix in the source code, but there is still no fixed version to install. MONAI Label is a server that research teams use to label medical scans and train imaging models; it is a separate program from the broader MONAI framework. The weakness is a path-traversal flaw in the parts of the server that store uploaded images and labels. item.title: Signal Blocks AI Agents From Reading Private Chats via Screenshots on Android and iOS
item.description: Signal has announced that it will restrict screenshots by default to stop artificial intelligence (AI) agents from reading private chats on Android and iOS devices, but conceded that the protection is "incomplete." The feature applies to agentic systems built into iOS 27 and on Android versions where the encrypted messaging platform can detect an AI assistant attempting to read the Signal screen. It also builds upon a similar setting that Signal introduced in Windows 11 last May following Microsoft's release of the controversial Recall feature. Calling the agentic integrations into Android, iOS, and Windows an "existential threat to Signal," Meredith Whittaker, president of the Signal Foundation, said the move is designed to uphold its privacy guarantees in the AI era.
